business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-China Free Trade Agreement (in force since 2014)
Switzerland-Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA), SR 951.0; Ordinance on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA-Ordinance), SR 951.01; Swiss Criminal Code, SR 311.0, arts. 305bis and 305ter; Code of Obligations, SR 220; Commercial Register Ordinance, SR 221.411; future central beneficial-owner register to be established under the Swiss Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities (Transparency Act), implementing ordinance pending.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or current extract from the commercial/corporate register of each corporate shareholder in the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or licensed corporate services provider in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each identified ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or passport-issuing authority in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds for the Swiss share capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the investor or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation if the founding shareholder is a legal entity signing through a representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, officer and authorized signatory against the consolidated SECO Swiss sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, EU/UK sanctions, FATF High-Risk Jurisdiction list and, where USD wire or escrow rails are used, the OFAC SDN list. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons under AMLA and applicable FINMA anti-money laundering guidelines. A written AML/CFT policy, verified UBO tree, source-of-funds documentary trail and negative media check must be completed before Swiss notarization; records must be retained for at least 10 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin characters. German, French, Italian or Romansh are the standard language options, but a name in another language may be accepted if it is clear and not misleading. The legal form indicator must be shown as 'AG' or 'SA'. Foreign-script names of UBOs and corporate shareholders must be transliterated into Latin script in the commercial register application; the transliteration must be certified by the notary where it affects the identity of a registered shareholder.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation may be extended before expiry by written application to the same cantonal Commercial Register Office. If the register office issues a formal name rejection, the applicant may request a written reasoned decision and file an objection with the cantonal Commercial Register Office within 30 days of notification. If the rejection is maintained, an appeal may be brought to the competent cantonal supervisory authority, with further recourse to the Federal Supreme Court as the final instance. A rejected name may be re-submitted after the impediment has been removed or after the statutory waiting period has elapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical Swiss registered office is mandatory. A pure virtual office without local management control is not permissible for a Swiss AG carrying on offshore platform supply vessel chartering, because statutory books, minutes, UBO register, accounting records and bank documentation must be accessible at the Swiss registered office. A licensed Swiss corporate services provider may supply the registered office, mail handling and statutory records location, but at least locally identifiable directors and commercial substance are required to support the maritime charter licence and escrow banking arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk of approximately 20% per financial year in the first three years; the likelihood rises to approximately 35% where the company is managed through a third-party registered office provider and does not maintain local board and commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name clearance and reservation fee at the cantonal Commercial Register Office via Zefix
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee tariff applicable under the Commercial Register Ordinance, SR 221.411; prevailing Zurich/Zug market rate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), Articles 620 to 763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Swiss Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HRA, SR 221.411), Articles 3, 4, 30; Swiss Civil Code (ZGB), Article 52 (legal personality).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug), Bahnhofstrasse 39, 6301 Zug, Switzerland.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Handelsregister-Anmeldung (Commercial Register Application) and Articles of Incorporation (Statuten).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an Aktiengesellschaft (AG), the statutory minimum share capital is CHF 100,000. At least CHF 50,000 must be paid up and deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a licensed Swiss bank; the bank's escrow attestation must be presented to the notary and the Commercial Register Office. Release of escrowed funds is only permitted after proof of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The shareholders having subscribed for the 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 par value each, the board confirms that the minimum capital of CHF 100,000 has been fully subscribed and the required CHF 50,000 paid-up portion is held in escrow with Zuger Kantonalbank. (2) The registered office is fixed at Bahnhofstrasse X, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. (3) The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Chairman, each with sole signatory authority for the company. (4) The officers are instructed to complete commercial register filing and obtain all operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Collect Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank in Canton Zug (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank) acting as escrow agent under OR Article 632.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and sign the escrow agreement; transfer at least CHF 50,000 from subscriber accounts to the blocked account; obtain the bank's attestation of capital availability (Freigabeerklärung). Confirm compliance with anti-money-laundering requirements for source of funds.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide supplementary tax and AML documentation; escalate to the bank's compliance officer for expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Founder Statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Notariat).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend notarial meeting physically or by remote certification under OR Article 590; have all founders declare their share subscriptions and adopt the Articles; obtain notarized minutes and a notarial certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Founder passport copies and proof of address
Value statement for non-cash contributions (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires further clarification on capital composition, submit a corrected draft or a legal memorandum explaining the treatment of any non-cash contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation with the Swiss Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed registration application via the Swiss commercial register portal (www.zefix.ch or eHRA) or in paper form; attach the notarized Articles, appointment resolution, specimen signatures, and escrow release waiver; pay the filing fee.
required_dossiers: Specimen signatures of board members and authorized officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (Rechtsverzögerung), respond with a supplementary memorandum and corrected forms within 10 days; request an expedited status review from the assigned registry case officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Company Identification Number and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and Compensation Fund of Canton Zug (AHV-Ausgleichskasse).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, the register office automatically transmits data to ESTV for issuance of the business identification number (UID). Subsequently register with the compensation fund for OASI/AVS social insurance and, if applicable, the cantonal tax office (Zug) for VAT and corporate income tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Board resolution on social insurance registration
Identification details of employees to be registered (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If UID issuance is delayed, contact ESTV's UID hotline for expedited handling; for social insurance, file a written objection within 30 days of any notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Maritime Navigation Office (Schweizerisches Seeschifffahrtsamt) within the Swiss Federal Office for Transport (FOT); for shore-based infrastructure, the Cantonal Building and Economic Development Department of Zug.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swiss Ship Operation License and Chartering Permit for Commercial Marine Services (Bewilligung zur gewerbsmässigen Seeschifffahrt)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN), Section for Environmental Assessments
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung) for vessel operations with fixed or mobile port infrastructure and recurring offshore discharges; simplified registration for pure vessel chartering without fixed Swiss installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Swiss Water Protection Act (GSchG) and MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I to V; discharge thresholds: BOD5 ≤ 20 mg/L, COD ≤ 60 mg/L, NH4-N ≤ 2 mg/L; VOC emissions not exceeding 150 g/m³ of crude oil/condensate; waste handling per Swiss Waste Ordinance (VVEA) and international maritime waste protocols.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for shore offices, fuel storage and quay facilities by the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate; structural load inspection of quays and cargo handling equipment by the Cantonal Building Authority; occupational health and safety clearance for marine crews and operations under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and the Maritime Labour Convention.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration ESTV (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni), online VAT and UID portal at www.estv.admin.ch, UID portal www.uid.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Swiss Aktiengesellschaft obtains a UID-MWST/TIN automatically in the commercial register; for foreign entity registration, application is made in writing to ESTV's VAT department using form 001; where the foreign enterprise has no Swiss place of business, a Swiss VAT representative is mandatory and the UID number is assigned by ESTV within the statutory processing window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; Swiss AG is per-se taxable. Available statutory elections include: small-business VAT exemption waiver under CHF 100k turnover, VAT grouping election, participation exemption election for qualifying dividends/capital gains, and Swiss hybrid-mismatch rules are mandatory. No general entity classification election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 Swiss Value Added Tax Act), including taxable supplies of goods and services; foreign entities only liable when that turnover is attributable to Switzerland, and must obtain a Swiss VAT number and appoint a fiscal representative if non-resident.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API validation is in force in Switzerland. Commercial invoices may be issued in paper or PDF; electronic invoicing is mandatory only for supplies to the federal administration (XML/eBill standards). Export proof and complete books and records must be retained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to the physical export of goods evidenced by Swiss customs export attestation (Art. 18 VAT Act) and to services directly ancillary to such export. An offshore supply-vessel charter may be zero-rated where the vessel is delivered outside Switzerland, used exclusively outside Swiss customs territory, or the lessee is established abroad and the operational use occurs beyond the Swiss continental shelf; place-of-supply rules and supporting documentation must conclusively demonstrate foreign use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / e-dec certified Customs Decision)
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill / Charter Party
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank proof of foreign payment settlement)
Vessel AIS/geolocation or voyage statements proving exclusive non-Swiss use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV audits exports with documentary substantiation; failure to justify zero-rating within the retention/export evidence period results in retrospective VAT assessment at 8.1% plus default interest. Knowingly false attestation of export or foreign use constitutes VAT evasion, triggering administrative fines of up to three times the tax evaded and criminal imprisonment under Art. 96/97 Swiss VAT Act; records must be retained ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) as central bank; foreign exchange regulation and financial market policy administered jointly by the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). Switzerland has no separate exchange-control authority and imposes no general restrictions on cross-border capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the OECD Code of Liberalisation. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely floating and freely convertible; no prior regulatory approval is required for foreign investment, dividend remittances, loan repayments, or profit repatriation. Dividend distributions by a Swiss AG are subject to a 35% Swiss withholding tax, which may be reduced to zero or a lower treaty rate if the beneficial owner provides proof of entitlement and the proper relief request is filed. Balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the SNB applies to banks and, at the Group level, to direct investment positions and cross-border financial assets/liabilities exceeding regulatory thresholds, but these are reporting obligations rather than convertibility controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters are free to maintain, invest, and repatriate proceeds in any convertible currency. There is no statutory time limit for repatriation; however, all cross-border receipts and payments must be routed through a licensed financial intermediary and are subject to Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act verification. For the offshore vessel leasing entity, transfer pricing documentation and contractual invoice terms must satisfy OECD arm's-length principles to avoid tax adjustments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) and multi-currency operational treasury account in CHF/EUR/USD
Capital Escrow Account and corporate operating account with dedicated SME and maritime-industry support desks
Capital Escrow Account and operating current account in CHF/EUR/USD; limited marine charter specialization
Private-banking relationship account and capital escrow account; not oriented to high-volume operational maritime disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability Rating: Low-Medium. Swiss-licensed EMIs and digital banks (fintech institutions under FINMA's FinTech Ordinance) and licensed payment institutions under FinIA can provide multi-currency IBANs, SWIFT access, and basic payment accounts. Legal constraints, however, are significant: (a) only a FINMA-licensed securities firm or bank may issue the escrow confirmation required by the Commercial Register for share capital deposits; (b) many EMIs explicitly exclude offshore marine clients as enhanced-risk and will not provide the capital-formation confirmation; (c) EEA/UK EMIs without a Swiss fintech license may not operate a Swiss-resident corporate payment account on a cross-border basis without FINMA authorization or a valid passporting arrangement; they may only offer ancillary FX services. Consequently, the principal operating treasury account should be established with a tier-1 Swiss bank; EMIs may be used as secondary FX conversion rails or for low-value disbursements only where they hold a FINMA license and accept the client risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an offshore supply-vessel leasing AG, a physical presence requirement generally applies to at least one authorised signatory and one director. Most tier-1 Swiss banks require an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Swiss head office or, where a bank has a qualified introducing-bank relationship abroad, at a foreign financial institution under a correspondent-bank protocol. Pure remote opening is possible only on a discretionary basis for low-risk private companies with substantive Swiss administration, notarized documentary packages, a video-identification process, and FINMA-compliant EDD; however, for offshore maritime operations the compliance committee will normally overrule remote processing. The share-capital escrow confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) is issued only by the licensed bank after the physical or equivalent verified interview is completed and all AML/KYC findings are cleared.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or directors are resident in a jurisdiction subject to FATF monitoring, a tax-haven blacklist, or PEP status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports and residence permits, source-of-wealth statements with certified bank statements for the last 12 months, tax residence certificates, CVs with clear business track record, PEP status declaration, independent wealth-management references from a regulated financial intermediary, and a formal legal opinion from Swiss counsel confirming the UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex corporate structure involving offshore shareholder vehicles, trusts, or foundations that obscure the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full consolidated organizational chart with shareholdings, trust deed or foundation instrument, UBO declaration in the form prescribed by Swiss banks, register of directors, notarized shareholder registry, Swiss legal opinion confirming the commercial purpose and economic rationale, and group audited financial statements for two prior years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore operating income derived from vessel charters or sub-charters to counterparties in high-risk maritime zones or with opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter-party agreements, pro-forma and commercial invoices, vessel registration documents with flag-state verification, IMO number, P&I insurance insurance certificates, vessel classification certificates, proof of ongoing statutory license under ISIC 5222, a detailed vessel deployment schedule, and a business-plan narrative setting out end-customer identities and trade flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share capital is sourced from irregular third-party payments or from a jurisdiction inconsistent with the investor's residence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement, bank reference letters from the remitting institution, source-of-funds declaration from each subscribing shareholder, copies of transfer-transaction advices showing the funds originate directly from the subscriber's own account, notarized deed of incorporation, and a sworn affidavit confirming no third-party payments are being made into the escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous tax residency of the entity or of directors, creating concern over unreported profits or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss canton tax certificate confirming corporate tax registration, Swiss federal tax identification, certificate of residence for each director, tax-clearance confirmations from previous jurisdictions, confirmatory tax rulings from the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and the relevant canton, and evidence that the company's management and economic substance are physically located in Switzerland.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the initial share-capital injection: (1) the AG's shareholders execute a notarized share subscription agreement in Switzerland; (2) each subscribing shareholder transfers funds from his/her own bank account to the 'Capital Escrow Account' (Sperrkonto) at the Swiss bank using SWIFT MT103 with the payment reference matching the subscription agreement and with a clear remittance purpose such as 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'CAPITAL INJECTION'; (3) the Swiss bank automatically tests the transaction under the Commercial Register framework and issues a legally valid escrow confirmation to the notary, attesting that the entire minimum capital (CHF 100,000 for an AG) is available and freely disposable by the signatories; (4) after the notarial deed is filed and the Commercial Register registers the AG, the account is unblocked and becomes the operational treasury account; (5) where capital is injected in foreign currency, conversion into CHF is recorded at the bank's spot rate and the origin of funds must be evidenced; (6) no payments from third parties except the registered subscriber are permitted, and the bank will reject misreference wires as 'unconfirmed capital'. For larger injections above the minimum capitalisation, the bank may request audited financial forecasts and evidence of the overall transaction structure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury settlements are executed through multiple rails: (a) Domestic CHF payments use the SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) system; (b) Euro-denominated trade and charter payments are cleared via SEPA and TARGET2-SECB (or EuroSIC) using MT103/MT202; (c) USD, GBP, NOK, and other freely convertible cross-border flows use SWIFT MT103/MT202 with standard clearing through the receiving bank's correspondent network; (d) commercial and standby letter-of-credit operations are issued as SWIFT MT700/MT760 under ICC UCP 600 and URDG 758 rules to secure shipyard instalments and charterer performance; (e) maritime-specific disbursements such as port dues, bunkering, crew wages, and vessel stores may be sent to designated agents through dedicated 'maritime clearing templates' or through an escrow-service agent using a dual-control payment instruction format; (f) the underlying outbound payment must be supported by the relevant charter contract, commercial invoice, customs declaration if physical goods move, and the SWIFT payment reference must align with BOP statistical categories (e.g., 'TRADE PAYMENT', 'SHIPPING FREIGHT', 'VESSEL OPERATIONS', 'CHARTER HIRE'). For all disbursements, the bank performs transaction monitoring and may block or suspend payments where the commercial documentation is incomplete or where the beneficial recipient does not match the trade party.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX outright forwards between CHF, EUR, USD, GBP, and other freely convertible currencies, tenors up to 12 months, documented under an ISDA/AMF master agreement or executed on a covered spot/forward basis with margin calls.
FX swaps and rolling forward contracts used for intra-company treasury repositioning, intercompany loan servicing, and precise management of charter-hire receipts against operating disbursements.

European-style currency options (call/put) with premium paid upfront, suitable for hedging forecasted charter income and lease payments in volatile but convertible currencies such as NOK, SGD, or ZAR; bank credit limits apply for maturities beyond 24 months.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) converting floating-rate USD lease receivables into fixed CHF or EUR rate exposures, matched to the underlying charter or leasing obligations.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) exclusively for currencies without a deliverable offshore market (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) to hedge contracted lease cash flows that cannot be settled onshore, subject to Swiss margin rules and FINMA conduct-of-business requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and approval of the annual financial statements under Articles 698–699 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate shareholders' assembly; no regulatory filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December balance-sheet date, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-sanctioned AGM at the company's expense, personal liability of the board of directors for damages; failure does not by itself trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined cantonal/federal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung der juristischen Personen)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax authority of the registered office and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the year following the tax period; standard extension to 30 September, and cantonal discretion for further extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest at the statutory annual rate, procedural fines (typically up to CHF 500), tax assessment on an estimated basis, and, in deliberate evasion cases, penalties of up to 100% of evaded tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each calendar quarter, or within 60 days after the end of the tax year if the taxpayer has been approved for annual VAT filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, VAT collection enforcement, administrative fines up to CHF 10,000, and tax-at-source measures in case of repeated non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit/review report (Jahresrechnung samt Revisionsbericht)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the AGM and, where required, the statutory auditor; no filing with the commercial register in ordinary non-listed cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared before the AGM and formally approved within six months after balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of profit distribution entitlement until approval, board and auditor civil liability, and enforcement of the right to AGM by court order; not a direct strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register (UBO) compliance review under Article 697j of the Swiss Code of Obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No authority filing; register must be kept at the registered office and produced to Swiss judicial, tax, and anti-money-laundering authorities on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing update obligation; annual verification at the latest at the AGM or at each transfer of shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Disciplinary fines under Article 697n CO, sanctions for providing false information to authorities, and increased criminal exposure under the Swiss AML framework for deliberate mistakes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (independent) audit is mandatory for Swiss AGs whose shares are listed, that are part of a consolidated-audit group, or that exceed two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20,000,000; total annual sales CHF 40,000,000; 250 average full-time employees. All other AGs require a limited review audit unless the unanimous shareholders' resolution opts out of audit when the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–962 CO); presentation may comply with Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is permitted, and is generally required for listed companies or consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland imposes no separate public annual UBO filing. The AG must maintain a beneficial-owner register at its registered office and update it immediately whenever share holdings or beneficial ownership changes. The annual compliance process consists of documenting board review and verification of the register at the AGM; authorities may request the register without prior notice.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Accounting books, vouchers and supporting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–4,000 per year for a Swiss registered office and administrative agent, depending on canton and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–12,000 for a limited review audit; USD 20,000–45,000 for an ordinary statutory audit of an active offshore-chartering AG

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined effective corporate income tax rate of approximately 11.6% to 11.9% in Canton Zug for an Aktiengesellschaft (federal direct tax at 8.5% of net after-tax profit, equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit, plus Zug cantonal and communal income tax of roughly 3.8% to 4.1%). The national statutory headline rate at the federal level only is 8.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation deduction of 100% for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from participations of at least 10% or a book value of CHF 1 million; Swiss patent box granting 90% exemption of qualifying patent income; R&D super-deduction of 150% of qualifying personnel and research costs; notional interest deduction on excess taxable equity granted in certain cantons including Zug; no tonnage or shipping-specific exemption applies to an offshore supply-vessel leasing AG, so ordinary income taxation applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income Tax Return for Legal Entities (Formular A / E-Form AJ for Aktiengesellschaften), filed electronically through the Canton Zug e-filing portal ('Digital Tax Zug') and the federal ESTV/SST software interface; the same return governs both the Direct Federal Tax (Wehrsteuer) and the Zug cantonal/communal taxes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; prepayments are imposed quarterly on the basis of the preceding year's assessment, with final reconciliation on the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by 31 March (paper) or 30 April (electronic filing) of the following year; an extension to 30 September is routinely granted upon request, and the statutory maximum deadline ends six months after the business year close pursuant to Art. 124-125 DBG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1101 - Balance Sheet Equity and Shareholders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of share capital, capital surplus, reserves, and interim equity changes; disclosure of all shareholders, including the foreign parent, its residence, and percentage holding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must be fully identified by name, domicile, and share percentage; attach the Articles of Association and share register excerpt; indicate any nominee arrangements, as nominee conduits will be attacked tax-wise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 1102 - Net Profit (Jahresgewinn) Before Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Audited commercial profit or loss for the year prepared under Swiss GAAP (FER) or IFRS, including charter hire revenue, bareboat leasing income, vessel operating expenses, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned AG, the entire Swiss commercial profit is reportable unless a permanent establishment abroad can be documented under an applicable double tax treaty; the Swiss economic nexus of charter decision-making must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 1103 - Tax Adjustments (Aufrechnungen und Kürzungen)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of non-deductible expenses added back (excess director fees, interest on shareholder loans above safe-haven ratios, non-business costs, deemed hidden distributions) and tax-deductible items removed (participation deduction, foreign PE income relief, arm's-length revaluations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident AGs must attach a transfer pricing summary for each intercompany transaction; management fees paid to a foreign affiliate are deductible only with a written agreement and evidence of actual services rendered in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of final chargeable profit applying all additions and deductions; this figure is the basis for federal and Zug cantonal/communal income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable profit must equal the arm's-length result for a Swiss profit centre; a loss-making Swiss AG operating in a high-margin global charter market will be interrogated and reallocated income under the Swiss TP doctrine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for 100% exemption of dividend and capital gains from qualifying participations of at least 10% or CHF 1 million carrying value, provided the shares are held as financial assets with holding intent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Qualification is denied if the Swiss AG is a pure letterbox or if the foreign participation serves solely to avoid Swiss taxes; the foreign operation must have actual substance and the Swiss AG must exercise genuine permanence of investment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the capital tax base at year-end, including paid-in share capital, open reserves, retained earnings, and hidden reserves; Canton Zug applies a capital tax of approximately 0.04% per year (rate varies with commune).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All share capital contributed by the non-resident parent counts in the taxable equity; systematic profit extraction leaving the AG with near-zero equity creates rebuttal risks of hidden equity injection and financing recharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 1107 - Withholding Tax and Distributions Recap
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all dividends, deemed distributions, interest on Swiss securities, and the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) actually remitted to the ESTV during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders are entitled only to treaty-reduced rates through the refund procedure; the AG must retain dividend vouchers and proof of WHT remittance to support the shareholder's reclaim; failure triggers strict joint liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers: (a) default interest of 3.5% per annum on the unpaid or reassessed tax; (b) procedural fines under Art. 173 DBG up to CHF 10,000 for failure to comply; (c) tax assessment under official estimation (Schätzung), reversing the burden of proof onto the taxpayer; (d) evasion penalties of 50% to 250% of the evaded tax under Art. 175 DBG for false or incomplete returns; (e) criminal tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG for forged documents, carrying imprisonment for the responsible individuals; (f) parallel cantonal fines in Zug and immediate debt collection (Betreibung) against the AG's assets upon default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on any dividend, constructive dividend, or value-shifting distribution made by the AG to its shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is procedural only, never a documentary exemption at payment. Protocol: (1) the AG pays the gross dividend and remits 35% to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); (2) the foreign parent obtains an original certificate of tax residence (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung / attestation de domicile) from its competent foreign tax authority; (3) within three years from the end of the calendar year of distribution, the parent files a treaty refund claim with the ESTV using the official DTA reclaim form, attaching the dividend voucher, proof of shareholding, and the residence certificate; (4) the ESTV refunds the excess of 35% over the treaty rate (typically 5% for a company holding directly at least 10% of the voting capital, otherwise 15% under most Swiss treaties; 0% under certain treaties for qualifying parent companies); (5) if the parent fails the beneficial-ownership or economic-substance test, the full 35% remains definitive and penalties may follow.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on ordinary commercial interest or on royalty/licence payments made by a Swiss AG to a foreign related party; the 35% Swiss withholding tax applies only to Swiss-issued bond or debenture interest and certain money-market paper. Under the OECD-based Swiss treaty network, royalties are tax-free at source (0%) and interest is generally tax-free at source (0%) except interest effectively connected to a Swiss permanent establishment or derived from Swiss-issued debt securities. Where domestic 35% was erroneously withheld, the same DTA refund procedure described for dividends applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Swiss Local File is mandatory when the Swiss AG has annual Swiss turnover above CHF 80 million or controlled intra-group transactions exceeding CHF 5 million per transaction category; a consolidated Master File is expected when the multinational group exceeds CHF 1 billion consolidated gross revenue. Even below these thresholds, ESTV practice requires a contemporaneous arm's-length benchmark for all major intercompany vessel charters, financing, and service arrangements.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - preferred for vessel time charter and bareboat lease rates benchmarked against Baltic Exchange indices and third-party charter fixtures
Resale Price Method - suitable for sub-chartering where the Swiss AG acts as an intermediary
Cost Plus Method - acceptable for technical management, crewing, and procurement services
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) - default method for network-profit testing of the Swiss leasing entity
Profit Split Method - applicable for integrated joint vessel ownership and jointly incurred marine operations
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no statutory Economic Substance Regulations analogous to the UAE ESR regime, but economic substance is enforced through: (1) the general anti-avoidance doctrine (Steuerumgehung) under Art. 210 DBG and settled Federal Supreme Court case law; (2) the sub-stance-over-form principle governing hidden equity and financing recharges; (3) the ESTV's transfer pricing and thin-capitalization safe-haven rules (debt-to-equity ratios for asset leasing, generally 6:1 to 8:1 for financed vessels with a requirement of arm's-length interest); and (4) treaty beneficial-ownership and Principal Purpose Test analysis. The offshore supply-vessel leasing AG must demonstrate genuine decision-making in Switzerland: board meetings actually held, charter contracts negotiated and signed in Switzerland, bank accounts and invoicing operated from Zug, the vessel registered in or managed through a substantive Swiss operation, and crew/insurance functions documented. A letterbox AG with all commercial decisions made overseas will lose treaty benefits, participation deduction, and may face deemed distributions of revenue to the true offshore manager.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion (Steuerhinterziehung) and Criminal Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating charter hire revenue, overstating vessel depreciation, mischaracterizing operating lease income as exempt participation income, omitting profit on vessel disposal, or submitting forged charter documents and false voyage records to the Zug tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment (Nachsteuer), default interest at 3.5% to 4% per annum, and an evasion penalty of 50% to 250% of the evaded federal tax under Art. 175-177 DBG, mirrored by cantonal penalties; criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG carries custodial sentencing for the individuals involved and limitation periods of 10 years (15 years for falsified books).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers responsible for the false filings are jointly liable for the corporate tax debt under Art. 12 DBG; the tax authority will issue a personal liability order (Haftungsverfügung), may assert civil restitution, attach personal bank accounts and real estate, impose travel bans during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment of up to three years per individual defendant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Withholding Tax Evasion and Abuse of DTA Refund
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying or declaring dividends to a foreign parent without withholding and remitting the 35% Swiss federal withholding tax, or structuring repatriations as untaxed management fees, rebates, or balance-sheet loans to circumvent WHT, or filing false DTA refund claims using fabricated residence certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the full 35% withholding tax from the AG, default interest, and administrative fines under the Swiss Withholding Tax Act (VStG); denial of all treaty relief for abusive arrangements and reclassification of the payment as a taxable constructive dividend at the full 35%; the transaction is 'versteuert' as if no treaty applied, plus procedural penalties and criminal monetary sanctions up to CHF 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the dividend resolution or authorize the non-withheld distribution are personally liable for the withheld amount and may be sued by the tax authority; criminal conviction for wilful non-collection carries imprisonment up to three years, and directors face confiscation of personal assets located in Switzerland and a prohibition from serving on Swiss boards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Missing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into intercompany vessel charter and bareboat arrangements with non-arm's-length rates, zero-rate management fees, undocumented cost allocations, missing local files above the CHF 80 million / CHF 5 million thresholds, or applying unsupported profit splits at year-end to deplete Swiss taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length profit, secondary adjustment classifying the excess as constructive dividend subject to 35% WHT, additional interest, and evasion penalties of up to 250% of the reassessed tax for intentional mispricing; incomplete documentation also triggers an official estimated assessment shifting the burden of proof to the taxpayer, alongside procedural fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the non-arm's-length pricing are jointly liable under Art. 12 DBG for the tax underpayment; the same facts may qualify as criminal tax fraud, leading to personal restitution claims, asset attachment, travel bans, and disqualification as bankruptcy trustees when the AG is rendered insolvent by the TP adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance (Letterbox AG)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Swiss AG without real employees, physical office, Swiss bank account, or board decision-making, while all charter negotiations, asset registries, crew management, and treasury decisions are made by a foreign offshore affiliate, solely to access the Swiss treaty network and participation deduction; also failing to adhere to safe-haven thin-capitalization ratios on vessel finance debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the Steuerumgehung (abuse) doctrine and refusal to respect the Swiss AG's separate legal status; denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, denial of the participation deduction, re-attribution of the full chartered income to the effective foreign beneficiary, and deemed distribution subject to 35% WHT; worse, the commercial register may order dissolution of the letterbox entity and retrospective tax assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors consenting to the shell arrangement face joint and several liability for all reclassified corporate taxes, personal fines for aiding tax violations, criminal prosecution for participation in a sham structure, and both civil and criminal seizure of personal property; the corporate veil is pierced, so the sole foreign shareholder is also directly liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Financing of Prohibited Operations (AML)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting charter payments in cash, cryptocurrency, or through undisclosed escrow conduits from high-risk ship operators or sanctioned jurisdictions, entering into fake vessel charters to move funds (round-tripping), failing to conduct beneficial-ownership due diligence on the ultimate vessel charterer, or co-mingling proprietary transactions with client funds in the same SWIFT/escrow accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions under Art. 305bis Swiss Penal Code: imprisonment up to three years and fines up to CHF 250,000; confiscation of the vessel and all traced proceeds (Art. 70 CP); administrative enforcement by the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and FINMA where applicable, including freezing orders on Swiss bank and escrow accounts; and an automatic 35% WHT re-characterization of suspicious distributions if round-tripping comes to light.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally prosecutable for money laundering where they knew or should have known of the illicit origins; penalties include custodial sentences, fines computed on the laundered value, asset confiscation, travel bans issued by the prosecutorial authorities, and civil compensation obligations; under the Swiss Code of Obligations, directors are also liable for the AG's consequent losses through breach of AML duties.
